mechanism: Both drugs cause CNS depression through different pathways (zolpidem via GABA-A agonism, fluphenazine via dopamine antagonism), with additive sedative and psychomotor effects; fluphenazine may inhibit metabolism of zolpidem via CYP3A4.
action: Monitor closely for excessive sedation, respiratory depression, and cognitive impairment; consider dose reduction of zolpidem; advise against concurrent use if possible; caution patients about fall risk and impaired coordination.
